title: Weather and seasons
description: Talk about a year of weather, from a heatwave to the first frost.
grammar: the future for a forecast, and the nouns of extreme weather
grammarNote: A forecast uses the future: mañana lloverá, it will rain tomorrow.

explanation.summary: A1 taught the weather as a fact: hace sol, hace frío. B1 turns it into a forecast and a year: what will happen, what season it belongs to, and what the extreme days are called.

sections.heading: The year in seasons
sections.body: La estación is one of the four parts of the year. El amanecer is when the day starts and el atardecer is when it ends. El rocío is the water on the grass in the morning, and it belongs to spring and autumn.

examples.es: La primavera es mi estación favorita.
El amanecer es a las siete.

examples.en: There is dew in the garden.

sections.heading: When the weather turns
sections.body: Una ola de calor is days of extreme heat, and la sequía is months without rain. La inundación is what a river does after a storm, and el granizo is ice falling from the sky. La niebla sits low over a town, and el arcoíris comes after the rain.

examples.es: Mañana habrá una ola de calor.
examples.en: There will be a heatwave tomorrow.

examples.es: La niebla no deja ver la calle.
examples.en: The fog does not let you see the street.

examples.es: Después de la tormenta salió el arcoíris.
examples.en: After the storm the rainbow came out.

items.note: Feminine: la estación. It also means the station.
Masculine: el rocío. The accent marks the stress.
Feminine: la sequía. The accent marks the stress.
Feminine: la inundación. The accent marks the stress.
Masculine: el arcoíris. The accent marks the stress.
